content: Nature gave us one tongue and two ears, so we could hear twice as much as we speak.
author: Zeno of Citium
sourceWork: Fragments of the Early Stoa (c. 300 BC)
story:
Shipwrecked off the coast of Attica and losing his entire cargo of Tyrian purple dye, Zeno wandered into a bookseller's shop in Athens, read Xenophon's Memorabilia of Socrates, and asked where such men could be found today. Walking to the Stoa Poikile (Painted Porch), he founded Stoicism, famously declaring: 'Now that I have been shipwrecked, I am on a good voyage.'

In formulating this reflection, Zeno of Citium stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of listening. For Zeno of Citium, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
